newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel bonds end higher in thin trading.
newsitem.headline: Israel bonds end higher in thin trading.

text.p: Israeli bond prices closed slightly higher on Wednesday with provident funds and portfolio managers trying to push the market upwards, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon - issued for four years): +0.12 pct to 167.42
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.12 pct at 159.12
Volume was low at 120 million shekels with most of the activity concentrated in unlinked bonds, traders said.
"The demand for long-term unlinked bonds continues. The main buyers were provident funds who are trying to show improved results at the end of the month," said Danni Scharia at Capital Securities.
"The dollar-linked bonds rose today because of the dollar's rise and the Makams (which are unlinked) also did well but total volume was relatively low," Scharia said.
The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2670 shekels against 3.2650 on Tuesday.
Long bonds linked to the consumer price index (CPI) also rose, continuing the trend of the past two months.

"The main reason for the rise of the long-term linked bonds is that there are simply no sellers and there is always a demand surplus, but the activity in those bonds was very low," said a trader at the First International Bank of Israel.

"The reaction of the dollar-linked bonds to the U.S. currency's rise was very moderate. Last week they did not react to the dollar's decline either. Portfolio managers together with provident funds who want to show improved results were trying to push the market," he added.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
